test_title: RRB NTPC CBT 2 (Level-6) Official paper (Held On: 9 May 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
From a rectangular metallic sheet of length 36 cm and breadth 16 cm, three circular plates of radii 6 cm, 4 cm and 2 cm are cut out. If the area of the remaining part of the metallic sheet is equal to the area of a square, then find the length of each side of the square (in cm).

( {Usespace pi = frac{{22}}{7}} )
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Sheet Area = 36 × 16 = 576 cm².

Sum of circle areas = (22/7) × (6² + 4² + 2²) = (22/7) × 56 = 176 cm².

Area of square = 576 − 176 = 400 cm².

Side of square = √400 = 20 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 20 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length (L) = 36 cm, Breadth (B) = 16 cm

Radii of 3 circles: r₁ = 6 cm, r₂ = 4 cm, r₃ = 2 cm

**Formula Used:**

**Area of Rectangle** = Length × Breadth

**Area of Circle** = π × r²

**Area of Square** = side²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/95c1bf637e444ab45c6d5da8b14ae6c17a7048b2499037bc7beb4d263fc182d1.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Area of **Rectangular Sheet** = 36 × 16 = 576 cm²

⇒ Total Area of 3 **Circular Plates** = π × (r₁² + r₂² + r₃²)

⇒ Area = (22/7) × (6² + 4² + 2²)

⇒ Area = (22/7) × (36 + 16 + 4) = (22/7) × 56

⇒ Area = 22 × 8 = 176 cm²

⇒ **Remaining Area** = Sheet Area − Total Circle Area

⇒ Remaining Area = 576 − 176 = 400 cm²

⇒ Area of **Square** = 400 cm²

⇒ side² = 400

⇒ side = √400 = 20 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 20 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of 2D Shapes

The **Area** of a rectangle is the product of its length and breadth (L × B). For a circle, the area is πr², where π ≈ 22/7.

Square Side Formula

If the **Area** of a square is known, the **length** of each side is the square root of the area (√Area).

Units of Measurement

Always ensure that all **dimensions** are in the same units (e.g., cm) before performing subtraction or comparison of areas.</p
